question.problem: Given that $h(x,y)=({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}){e}^{x}$, find the points $(x,y)$ where $∇h(x,y)=0.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}){e}^{x}) \\  & =2x{e}^{x}+({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}){e}^{x} \\  & =({x}^{2}+2x-{y}^{2}){e}^{x} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}){e}^{x}) \\  & =-2y{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $∇h(x,y)=({x}^{2}+2x-{y}^{2}){e}^{x}\,i-2y{e}^{x}\,j.$

Now, we solve $∇h(x,y)=0:$

$$
({x}^{2}+2x-{y}^{2}){e}^{x}\,i-2y{e}^{x}\,j=0\text{ }i+0\text{ }j
$$

So, by equating the coefficients of $i$ and $j,$ we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}+2x-{y}^{2}){e}^{x}=0, \\ -2y{e}^{x}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $y=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}+2x-{0}^{2}){e}^{x} & =0 \\ x(x+2){e}^{x} & =0 \\ x & =-2,\,0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $∇h(x,y)=0$ at two points: $(-2,0)$ and $(0,0).$
